node.label: Paul Veyne
node.date_label: Comment on écrit l’histoire (1971) · Le Pain et le Cirque (1976) · Les Grecs ont-ils cru à leurs mythes? (1983)
node.description: A historian of the ancient world who also asks how historians select and explain events. In the selected methodological extract, an event gains relevance within a chosen inquiry, but that choice does not make the relations within it arbitrary. His concept of intrigue can include several temporal rhythms and need not follow a simple chronological sequence. The map compares that position with the later narrative debate without asserting a historical transmission or treating historical narrative as licensed fiction.

verification.note: Fresh selected authorial body passages through a public third-party transcription: introduction; chapter 3 Pas de faits sans questions; chapter 8 causal imagination, experience/expectation and uncertainty; chapter 10 Labroussian paradigm; chapter 11 White’s typologies and prefiguration; chapter 12 de Certeau and citation. The ISBN was read in the digital frontmatter and independently matched to BAnQ institutional metadata https://banq.pretnumerique.ca/v1/resources/541c 419c 96c 235e8f 1004686?l=en (April 2014, expanded by two articles). Copyright 1996, 2010 is not an assertion that all consulted wording dates to 1996. Use chapter/section/paragraph locators; tool line numbers and reflowed 456-page host count are not original print pagination. No print-facsimile collation, complete-book reading or fresh reading of the quoted authors’ originals. Publisher/Cairn access failures do not count as body witnesses. Earlier Agulhon/Voldman reviews retain their exact mediation and original-edition limits.
